claim: ELI5: the grader changed its mind about what counts as winning, and almost nothing in the campaign has caught up to that yet. Until now the goal was 'match the 89-92% reference state as closely as you can', and cycle 13 finally did it: it reproduced the campaign's own sealed anchor fidelity to about two ten-thousandths, which also proved (measured, not argued) that the target construction taken straight from the contract's Metric line is the right one. The new goal is different and harder to fake: reaching the anchor fidelity is now worth zero credit by itself, and the only thing scored is HOW CHEAP the circuit is that reaches it. Cost here means the number of two-qubit entangling gates, the expensive ones on real hardware. The reference circuit spends exactly 35 of them. So the question this cycle asks is the simplest possible version of the campaign's actual scientific question: are all 35 of those gates actually doing work, or is the reference wasteful? The way to find out is to delete them one at a time. Take the reference circuit, try removing each single two-qubit gate, re-tune the 96 rotation knobs around the hole, and keep the deletion that hurts least. If the re-tuned circuit still reaches anchor fidelity, the gate was waste: accept the deletion and try again on what is left. Stop the first time no single remaining gate can be removed without dropping below the anchor. The number of gates left at that moment IS the answer the contract asks for, the cheapest preparation that still reaches anchor fidelity, and the trace of (cost, fidelity) pairs collected on the way down IS the fidelity-vs-cost curve the contract wants recorded. Why this and not the paper's ma-QAOA + SAP/OSAP route first: I priced that route analytically before proposing anything, and it does not fit through the door yet. Each of the 2K = 24 four-body Pauli strings in H_cost costs 6 CNOTs to exponentiate (2(w-1) for weight w = 4), so ONE ma-QAOA layer costs about 144 two-qubit gates plus 1 for the |I> reference. The contract declares anything above 70 INVALID, so an un-pruned p = 1 ma-QAOA candidate cannot even be scored: it needs roughly 80% of its terms pruned away just to become a legal submission, and roughly 96% pruned (about 5 surviving four-body terms) to land under 35. That is a real and interesting measurement, but it is a large search and it must not be the first thing attempted under a metric no candidate has ever been scored against. This cycle buys the cheap, decisive bit first: whether the 35-gate anchor circuit is itself compressible, on the one structure family the campaign has already validated end to end. Formally: branching from EXP-0013, the candidate rebuilds the target unchanged (H_tot dense from payload['h_cost'] with leftmost Pauli label character = qubit 0, T = normalize(expm(-beta*H_tot/4) @ payload['reference_state']) at beta = payload['beta'], which is CONTRACT.md's frozen Metric line read literally and needs no Majorana algebra, no Jordan-Wigner choice and no kernel solve), then runs greedy backward elimination over a boolean mask on the 35 CNOT slots of the hardware-efficient block (6 layers of rz/rx on 8 qubits interleaved with 5 linear chains cx(q,q+1), q = 0..6, after layers 0..4), with the contract-mandated 8-Hadamard prefix that costs 0 on the two-qubit axis, refitting theta of shape (6,8,2) by adjoint-gradient L-BFGS-B at every tentative removal, accepting a removal only when the refit self-fit fidelity clears the CONTRACT-published per-instance anchor F35 plus a 0.002 margin, under a wall-clock deadline guard that always returns a valid circuit. The structural change is deliberate and is the whole hypothesis: the incumbent's byte-identical-topology constraint, correct for confirming the convention, is exactly what the new metric makes worthless, so it is dropped here for the first time.
prediction: Under the revised mechanism-discriminating metric (s_i = 1000*max(0, F35_i - F_i) + C2_i, score = mean_i s_i), greedy CNOT elimination with refit reaches F_i >= F35_i on ALL FIVE instances at a mean two-qubit cost strictly below 35, giving mean score <= 30.0 (i.e. at least 5 of the 35 CNOTs are prunable on average with zero fidelity debt), and therefore satisfying the contract's ship condition (mean score <= 33.0, every instance F >= F35 and C2 < 35). Directional sub-prediction, advisory and recorded either way: the crossing cost is instance-dependent and lands in the range 20 to 32 CNOTs, and the accepted-removal trace is monotone in the sense that the last few removals each cost more fidelity than the first few (the early removals are near-free waste, the late ones are load-bearing entanglement). Stated as the incumbent delta: the incumbent (EXP-0013 refit at the full 35-CNOT structure) scores approximately 35.2 under the revised metric (cost 35 plus the roughly 0.0002 mean fidelity debt its own score implies, 1000x weighted), so the predicted improvement is at least 5 points.
falsifier: On at least one of the five instances, NO single CNOT can be removed from the full 35-slot structure while the refitted circuit still reaches F >= F35(instance) + 0.002, with that instance's full-structure baseline fit itself clearing the anchor (so the failure is attributable to structure, not to a failed fit). That instance's crossing cost is then exactly 35 and the 35-CNOT block is cost-optimal within its own family at beta = 3 on that instance. Distinguishing observation that must be recorded to make the falsification legitimate: for each of the 35 first-round tentative removals, the best refit fidelity reached and its L-BFGS-B termination record (status, nit, nfev, final gradient infinity-norm), so that 'removal genuinely destroys fidelity' (best first-round refit F below F35 - 0.01, converged) is separated from 'the warm-started refit never converged' (best first-round refit within 0.005 of the anchor with status = maxiter or gradient norm above 1e-6). The second case is NOT a falsification: it is an under-optimization finding and it fires the reopen condition instead.
kill_threshold: Mean score >= 34.9 with all five instances' full-structure fits clearing their anchors and all first-round tentative refits recorded as CONVERGED (status 0 or gradient infinity-norm <= 1e-6). That is fewer than 0.1 CNOTs saved per instance on average with no optimizer excuse available, and it kills the direction 'structural pruning of the hardware-efficient 35-CNOT block' as a route to a cheaper anchor-reaching preparation: the block is minimal at 35 in its own family, the crossing cost on the logical axis is 35, and the campaign's remaining options are the ma-QAOA + SAP/OSAP axis (which must first solve the 145-to-35 legality gap priced in the claim) or shipping the certified matched-cost null as QUESTION-STATUS with 35 recorded as the block-family crossing cost. Accept the kill when it fires; do not propose a variant of block pruning in cycle 15 if it does.
brief:
TARGET FILE: workspace/candidate.py (the ONLY editable file; a diff touching anything else is a rejection). Full rewrite of that one file is expected and authorized: the pruning machinery replaces the fixed-topology emitter, so most of the file changes. Do not create candidate_v2.py or any sibling. Do not read, open, list or glob anything under scorekeeper_private/. Do not import the target from anywhere; it is built from the payload.

PARENT: EXP-0013 (archived). Reuse its target construction, its simulator and its adjoint gradient VERBATIM where they exist; if the archived file is available at campaigns/syk-tfd-prune/state or via the harness archive, copy those three components rather than re-deriving them. They are measured-correct: EXP-0013's score of 8.849 under the old metric (100*(1-F) + cost penalty) implies mean F = 0.91151 against a mean anchor of 0.91174, i.e. the target construction reproduces the sealed anchor to 2.3e-4. Nothing about the target is an open question in this cycle.

--- SECTION 0: MODULE CONTRACT ---
Define prepare(payload) -> dict returning {'n_qubits': 8, 'gates': [...], 'diagnostics': {...}}. Only 'n_qubits' and 'gates' are read by the scorer; 'diagnostics' is advisory and must never be required for correctness. Gate dicts are exactly {'name': str, 'qubits': [int, ...], 'param': float}. Only these gate names are emitted: 'h' (1q), 'rz' (1q), 'rx' (1q), 'cx' (2q, qubits[0] = control). Logical two-qubit cost is therefore exactly the number of 'cx' gates.

--- SECTION 1: TARGET CONSTRUCTION (committed unconditionally, no alternatives, no switching) ---
1.1 Build H_tot as a dense 256x256 complex matrix from payload['h_cost']: for each (label, coeff) pair, label is an 8-character Pauli string over {I,X,Y,Z}; the LEFTMOST character is qubit 0 and qubit 0 is the MOST SIGNIFICANT bit of the 256-dimensional index. Build the operator as the Kronecker product in label order (kron(P_label[0], P_label[1], ..., P_label[7])) and accumulate coeff * that.
1.2 Assert Hermiticity: np.max(np.abs(H_tot - H_tot.conj().T)) < 1e-9. On failure raise immediately (import-time-class error, not a silent fallback).
1.3 beta = float(payload['beta']). T_raw = scipy.linalg.expm(-beta * H_tot / 4.0) @ np.asarray(payload['reference_state'], dtype=complex).ravel(). Assert T_raw.shape == (256,) and np.linalg.norm(T_raw) > 1e-12. T = T_raw / np.linalg.norm(T_raw).
1.4 No gauge fix is applied and none is needed: fidelity |<T|psi>|^2 is phase-blind. Do not enumerate alternative constructions, do not compute cross-overlaps against variants, do not branch on any of them. That machinery belonged to the convention-identification cycles and is now dead weight; the convention is measured.

--- SECTION 2: BLOCK BUILDER WITH A CNOT MASK ---
2.1 Constants, transcribed from workspace/baseline.py: LAYERS = 6, N_CHAINS = 5, BLOCK_QUBITS = 8, ANGLE_SEED = 0. The full block emits, for layer in range(6): for q in range(8): rz(q, theta[layer, q, 0]) then rx(q, theta[layer, q, 1]); then, if layer < N_CHAINS: for q in range(7): cx(q, q+1). Total 96 rotations + 35 cx = 131 gates, exactly 35 logical CNOTs, no 'h' anywhere.
2.2 The 35 CNOT slots are indexed in EMISSION ORDER: slot s = 7*layer + q for layer in 0..4, q in 0..6. Write masked_block_gates(theta, mask) where mask is a length-35 boolean array; a cx is emitted iff mask[s] is True. Rotations are always emitted regardless of mask.
2.3 IMPORT-TIME TOPOLOGY GATE (mandatory, non-negotiable): insert the repo's workspace directory on sys.path, import baseline, and assert that masked_block_gates(theta_ref, np.ones(35, bool)) equals baseline.block_gates(theta_ref) element-for-element (same length, same 'name', same 'qubits' list, same 'param' to within 0.0) for theta_ref = baseline.block_angles(). If the import raises ImportError, fall back to a verbatim inlined transcription of baseline.block_angles / block_gates included in this file, and record diagnostics['baseline_import'] = 'inlined_fallback'; do NOT skip the assertion in that case, run it against the inlined copy. If the assertion itself fails, raise: the structure premise is broken and no result from this cycle would be interpretable.
2.4 EMITTED CIRCUIT = eight h gates on qubits 0..7 (in ascending qubit order) followed by masked_block_gates(theta, mask). CONTRACT.md mandates the Hadamard prefix twice verbatim ('the 35-CNOT baseline via 8 Hadamards to |+>^8'; 'prepare your own reference: 8 H for the hardware-efficient block') and the sealed anchor was measured on the prefixed circuit. Hadamards are one-qubit gates, so the prefix costs exactly 0 on the scored two-qubit axis. Never emit the bare block.

--- SECTION 3: SIMULATOR AND ADJOINT GRADIENT ---
3.1 State is a complex vector of length 256, qubit 0 most significant. Apply gates by reshaping to (2,)*8 and contracting the 2x2 (or 4x4 / controlled) matrix on the relevant axis or axes; do not build 256x256 gate matrices.
3.2 Rotation convention: rz(t) = expm(-i*t*Z/2), rx(t) = expm(-i*t*X/2), matching CONTRACT.md's 'Rotations use exp(-i*theta*P/2)'.
3.3 Objective: psi(theta) = U(theta) |+>^8 where |+>^8 is computed ONCE per prepare call and cached (it is theta-independent). F(theta) = |<T|psi>|^2. Minimize f = -F.
3.4 Gradient by the accumulate-then-undo adjoint: forward-simulate once from the cached |+>^8 storing nothing but the final state; set the co-state lambda = <T|psi> * T (so that d f / d psi* gives the right contraction), then walk the gate list BACKWARDS, at each step applying the inverse gate to both psi and lambda, and for each parametrized gate accumulate dF/dtheta_k = 2 * Re( lambda_after^dagger (-i P / 2) psi_after ) with the sign consistent with f = -F. Derive the exact expression in code and then PROVE it numerically rather than trusting the derivation.
3.5 IMPORT-TIME FINITE-DIFFERENCE GATE (mandatory): with a random 256-dim normalized T from default_rng(7), a random theta from default_rng(8) uniform in [-pi, pi], and a random mask from default_rng(9) with 20 True slots, compare the analytic gradient against central finite differences (h = 1e-6) on 6 randomly chosen coordinates; assert max absolute difference < 1e-6. If it fails, raise. The whole cycle's cost depends on gradient correctness under a NON-FULL mask, which is new in this cycle, so the gate must run with a non-trivial mask, not just the all-True one.

--- SECTION 4: THE ANCHOR TABLE (public contract data, not battery data) ---
4.1 ANCHOR = {'INST-A': 0.8955, 'INST-B': 0.9164, 'INST-C': 0.9011, 'INST-D': 0.9228, 'INST-E': 0.9229}, transcribed verbatim from CONTRACT.md's Metric paragraph ('the sealed per-instance F35 (0.8955 Row 42, 0.9164 Row 48, 0.9011 Row 32, 0.9228 Row 30, 0.9229 Eq. 11)') under the contract's own mapping 'INST-A..E = Row 42/48/32/30, Eq. 11'. These numbers are published in the PUBLIC contract; reading them is not battery access and no hidden test is being inferred. Do not attempt to locate, recompute or refine the sealed values.
4.2 MARGIN = 0.002. Acceptance threshold for instance name: THRESH = ANCHOR[name] + MARGIN. The margin covers the contract's 4-decimal rounding (at most 5e-5) with three orders of magnitude of headroom and buys the 1000x-weighted fidelity term a safety buffer; a 0.002 fidelity surplus is worth 2 score points of insurance against a debt that would cost far more.
4.3 If payload['name'] is not a key of ANCHOR, set THRESH = max(ANCHOR.values()) + MARGIN = 0.9249 (conservative for every instance) and record diagnostics['unknown_instance'] = name. Never default to a LOWER threshold.

--- SECTION 5: FIT PRIMITIVE ---
5.1 fit(theta0, mask, maxiter, n_restarts, restart_seed) -> (best_theta, best_F, records): run scipy.optimize.minimize(method='L-BFGS-B', jac=analytic, options={'maxiter': maxiter, 'ftol': 0.0, 'gtol': 1e-10}) from theta0 flattened, then from (n_restarts - 1) additional starts drawn uniform in [-pi, pi] from default_rng(restart_seed); return the argmax over F. records is a list of dicts per start: {'F', 'status', 'message', 'nit', 'nfev', 'gmax'} where gmax is the final gradient infinity-norm.
5.2 FULL-STRUCTURE BASELINE FIT (per instance, run first): theta0 = baseline.block_angles() (or the inlined equivalent), mask = all True, maxiter = 3000, n_restarts = 8, restart_seed = 0. Record F_full and its records as diagnostics['full_structure']. This must reach at least ANCHOR[name] - 0.001; if it does not, SKIP pruning entirely, return the full-structure best circuit, and set diagnostics['abort_reason'] = 'full_structure_fit_below_anchor'. A pruning result obtained under a fit that cannot even reproduce the anchor at full structure is uninterpretable, and the falsifier explicitly requires this guard.
5.3 TENTATIVE REFIT (inside a greedy round): warm start from the current accepted theta ONLY, n_restarts = 1, maxiter = 400.
5.4 CONSOLIDATION FIT (after a removal is accepted): theta0 = the tentative winner's theta, n_restarts = 4 (warm start plus 3 random), restart_seed = 500 + current_cost, maxiter = 1500. The consolidated theta and F become the new accepted state. A removal is only FINALLY accepted if the consolidated F >= THRESH; if consolidation lands below THRESH (possible in principle, since the tentative refit had fewer iterations, though it starts from a point already above THRESH so this should not fire), revert the removal and stop the loop with diagnostics['stop_reason'] = 'consolidation_regression'.

--- SECTION 6: GREEDY BACKWARD ELIMINATION ---
6.1 State: mask (starts all True), theta (starts at the Section 5.2 winner), cost = mask.sum(), F = F_full.
6.2 Round: for every slot s with mask[s] True, in ascending s, form trial_mask = mask with s set False, run the Section 5.3 tentative refit, and record (s, F_trial, termination record). Keep the argmax over F_trial.
6.3 If the best F_trial >= THRESH: remove that slot, run the Section 5.4 consolidation, append (cost_after, F_after, removed_slot) to the trace, and start a new round. Otherwise stop with diagnostics['stop_reason'] = 'no_acceptable_removal' and keep the LAST ACCEPTED (mask, theta).
6.4 Also stop if cost reaches 0. Do not impose any other floor: let the data decide where the crossing is.
6.5 The FIRST round's complete 35-entry table (slot, best F_trial, status, nit, nfev, gmax) MUST be stored in diagnostics['round1_table'] verbatim. The falsifier's converged-vs-under-optimized distinction is read off exactly this table, so it is not optional and must be recorded even when pruning succeeds.
6.6 Complexity sanity: at most 35 + 34 + ... = 630 tentative refits per instance, each roughly 400 L-BFGS-B iterations over a 139-gate, 256-dimensional circuit. Measure the wall time of ONE tentative refit at the start of the first round and record it as diagnostics['refit_seconds']. If 630 * refit_seconds would exceed the deadline, that is fine, the deadline guard handles it; do not silently reduce maxiter.

--- SECTION 7: DEADLINE GUARD (the cycle must always produce a scored verdict) ---
7.1 DEADLINE_S = 240.0 per prepare() call, measured from function entry with time.monotonic().
7.2 Check the deadline at the top of every tentative refit. On exceedance, break out of the greedy loop immediately, keep the last accepted (mask, theta), and set diagnostics['stop_reason'] = 'deadline'. A partially-completed round contributes nothing: never accept a removal from an incomplete round unless every surviving slot in that round was tried.
7.3 Wrap the ENTIRE body of prepare() in try/except Exception. On any exception, return the full 35-CNOT structure at the best theta found so far (or at baseline.block_angles() if the fit never produced one), with diagnostics['guard'] = repr(exc) and diagnostics['guard_traceback'] = the formatted traceback. The fallback must be a valid 139-gate, 35-cx circuit. A crashed cycle teaches nothing; a guarded cycle that returns the incumbent circuit with a recorded reason keeps the ledger honest for the price of one scored run.
7.4 The returned circuit must ALWAYS satisfy: len(gates) <= 5000, cx count <= 35, every qubit index in 0..7, every 'cx' with two distinct qubits. Assert all four before returning.

--- SECTION 8: DIAGNOSTICS AND REPORTING (advisory only; the scorer reads nothing here) ---
8.1 diagnostics per instance must contain: name, THRESH, F_full and its 8 termination records, refit_seconds, round1_table (35 entries), the accepted trace as a list of (cost, F) pairs from 35 down to the final cost, final_cost, final_F_self, stop_reason, and any guard/abort fields. The trace IS the fidelity-vs-cost curve on the block family that CONTRACT.md asks to be recorded per instance.
8.2 Print exactly one line per instance to stdout of the form 'DIAG <json>' with that dict, so the coder's report and the journal entry can carry the curve. No other printing.
8.3 EVERY number in diagnostics is self-reported and advisory (rule 3). Do not state any of them as a score, do not compare them to the incumbent's score, and do not write to PRIORS or any verdict file.

--- SECTION 9: EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE THIS CYCLE (do not implement, do not 'improve') ---
No ma-QAOA ansatz, no SAP/OSAP over ma-QAOA angles, no alternative target constructions or cross-overlap tables, no agreement test against the scorer's per-instance penalty, no encoding enumeration, no routed-axis computation, no gate set beyond h/rz/rx/cx, no change to LAYERS/N_CHAINS/BLOCK_QUBITS, no reordering or relocation of CNOT slots (removal only, never insertion or movement), no per-instance special casing beyond the ANCHOR lookup. One hypothesis per change: this cycle changes the STRUCTURE SEARCH and nothing else.
done_definition: DONE when ALL of the following hold. (1) Only workspace/candidate.py is modified in the diff; nothing under scorekeeper_private/ was read, opened, globbed or listed. (2) Importing workspace/candidate.py runs and PASSES both mandatory gates: the Section 2.3 element-for-element topology identity against baseline.block_gates (or its verbatim inlined fallback) at mask = all True, and the Section 3.5 finite-difference gradient check under a 20-slot non-full mask with max absolute deviation < 1e-6. (3) prepare(payload) returns a dict with 'n_qubits' == 8 and a gate list whose every entry uses only h/rz/rx/cx with valid qubit indices, whose cx count is <= 35, and whose length is <= 5000, for every one of the five instance names, within the 240 s per-call deadline, with no uncaught exception. (4) The emitted circuit begins with eight h gates on qubits 0..7 and continues with masked_block_gates at the fitted theta, so the Hadamard prefix is present and the two-qubit cost equals the surviving cx count exactly. (5) Per instance, diagnostics carries the full-structure fit F_full with all 8 termination records, the complete 35-entry round-1 table with (slot, best F_trial, status, nit, nfev, gmax), the accepted (cost, F) trace, final_cost, final_F_self and stop_reason, and one 'DIAG <json>' line was printed per instance. (6) Either every accepted structure's consolidated self-fit F >= ANCHOR[name] + 0.002, or the candidate fell back to the full 35-CNOT structure with an explicit abort_reason / stop_reason / guard field recorded. (7) The coder's report states, per instance, final_cost and final_F_self and stop_reason as SELF-REPORTED advisory numbers, makes no claim about the score, and does not touch PRIORS, DIRECTION, CONTRACT or any verdict file.
reopen_condition: The direction 'structural pruning of the hardware-efficient 35-CNOT block' reopens on exactly one of three priced facts, each a measurement, not a re-argument. (A) UNDER-OPTIMIZATION SHOWN: the round-1 table from this cycle contains at least one slot whose best tentative refit reached within 0.005 of THRESH with a termination record of status = maxiter or gmax > 1e-6, AND a follow-up study on that single slot alone, at 24 restarts x 3000 L-BFGS-B iterations (default_rng(2000 + slot), same ftol 0 / gtol 1e-10), pushes it to or above THRESH. Cost: one cheap offline slot study, no scored run needed to decide. That fact means the crossing was set by the 400-iteration warm-start budget rather than by the structure, and the greedy loop reruns with maxiter raised to the level the study needed. (B) ANCHOR MOVED DOWN: the sealed per-instance F35 is re-sealed at least 0.01 BELOW its currently published value on any instance (e.g. via the contract's pre-registered baseline-fairness escalation, or a Director revision of the baseline refit). A 0.01 lower anchor mechanically moves the crossing cost down and can turn a 35 into a sub-35 on that instance without any change to the search. (C) STRUCTURE FAMILY WIDENED BY A MEASURED RESULT: a sibling or published result exhibits an 8-qubit, <= 35-CNOT circuit reaching F >= 0.92 on any of these five instances at beta = 3 with a connectivity pattern not reachable by DELETING slots from the 5-linear-chain block (for instance a non-nearest-neighbour or reordered chain), in which case the reopened direction is removal-plus-relocation rather than removal-only, and it reopens as a NEW hypothesis with its own pre-registration rather than as a retry of this one. Absent A, B or C, a kill here is final and the campaign goes to the ma-QAOA + SAP/OSAP axis (which must first close the 145-CNOT-to-35 legality gap priced in the claim) or ships the certified matched-cost null as QUESTION-STATUS with 35 recorded as the block-family crossing cost.
